audienceEvidence.countMeaning: Tagged article count, not readership or reachable parents.
audienceEvidence.selection: First four entries in the new-article list, not selected by high likes.
audienceEvidence.limitation: Only list titles, relative ages and displayed likes inspected. Readers' parental status and referral outcomes unknown. No platform-wide average inferred.

decisionRules: With negligible article exposure, check visibility and topic fit, then stop duplicating the same article format and reassess the next route.
With exposure but few visits, consider one title or cover change and record the change time.
With visits but no confirmed YouTube viewing, inspect embed and invitation, change one element and review after another seven days.
With reported YouTube referrals or useful article response, assess counts, viewing quality and total effort before a second article using the rain video.
Suppressed or delayed analytics mean unknown, not zero impact. Small sequential trials do not establish comparative causality. No automatic advertising transition.

notes: Do not add external video views to YouTube views.
note browser analytics distinguish impressions and page views as of September 2026. Neither is a YouTube view, and PV divided by internal impressions is not a strict click-through rate.

Record YouTube external sources and playback quality only where the actual UI reports them. Source-attributed repeat viewing is unknown unless directly reported; the paid-promotion follow-on metric is not assumed available for this organic pilot.
Capture a pre-publication baseline and annotate external publication overlap with the existing YouTube observations. Do not replace their strict 24/72-hour checkpoints.
No cross-platform deduplication or causal attribution claimed.

Create deadlines only after real publication. Align the existing monitor with the actual external deadlines if needed; capture actual elapsed time and never backfill a missed checkpoint with later values.
